governing_table.code: 2018 North Carolina Plumbing Code (based on the 2015 International Plumbing Code), with Building Code Council amendments through December 2024; repeated as Table 2902.1 of the 2018 North Carolina Building Code
governing_table.edition: 2018 NC code, effective January 1, 2019; office row as amended effective January 1, 2021
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures (Building Code Table 2902.1)
governing_table.quote: 2018 NC Plumbing Code (based on the 2015 International Plumbing Code) effective 1/1/2019 ... 403.1 Minimum Number of Fixtures. In new construction or building additions and in changes of occupancy as defined in the North Carolina Building Code, plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1 based on the actual use of the building or space.

cities_may_amend_note.text: The State Building Code applies statewide; a city or county may adopt only a fire prevention code and floodplain rules, and those need Code Council approval. So Charlotte, Durham, Greensboro and Raleigh use the state table unamended.
cities_may_amend_note.quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the North Carolina State Building Code shall apply throughout the State, from the time of its adoption. ... However, any political subdivision of the State may adopt a fire prevention code and floodplain management regulations within its jurisdiction.

office.row_label: 2 Business, B: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 30 for the first 30 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 30
office.wc_female: 1 per 30 for the first 30 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 30
office.urinals: None in the table; heading reads 'URINALS: SEE SECTION 419.2'
office.quote: Business ... B ... 1 per 30 for the first 30 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 30 [water closets, one cell across male and female] | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 [lavatories] ... The delayed effective date of this Rule is January 1, 2021.
office.note: Read on the official OSFM amendments PDF (item 191210 B-18 and B-20), which shows 25 and 50 struck through and replaced by 30.

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly, A-2: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts
restaurant.urinals: None in the table; see Section 419.2
restaurant.quote: A-2 ... Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 | — | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink
restaurant.note: Read on UpCodes (secondary copy); the official ICC copy is behind a captcha. Footnote d: 'The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.'

school.urinals: None in the table; see Section 419.2 and, for public schools, Section 403.8.5.3
school.quote: Educational | E b, i | K-8 9-12 Teacher/staff | 1 per 25 1 per 30 1 per 30 | 1 per 25 1 per 25 1 per 25 | 1 per 60 1 per 100 1 per 100 | — | 1 per 100 ... i. See Section 403.8 for additional information on plumbing fixtures for schools.
school.note: Read on UpCodes (secondary copy). The same row appears in Building Code Table 2902.1.

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistical data shows another split. Public school staff are split 80% female / 20% male (K-8) and 70% / 30% (9-12).
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: 1. The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number; for mixed occupancies the fractions are summed first, then rounded up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly and educational occupancies and up to 50% elsewhere. Public schools: urinals may replace toilets in male group toilet rooms for staff, gyms, auditoriums, cafeterias and stadiums, but toilets may not fall below one third of the flushing fixtures; a four-fixture male group toilet needs at least two toilets. Each urinal needs a privacy partition.
urinal_substitution.quote: 419.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. ... 403.8.5.3 Substitutions. Water closets may be substituted for urinals for grades K through 2. Urinals may be substituted for water closets in male group toilet rooms for teachers/staff and gyms, auditoriums, cafeterias or stadiums. The number of water closets shall not be reduced to less than one-third of the required total number of flushing fixtures.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required in an office (business occupancy) with 30 or fewer occupants, in any other building or tenant space with 25 or fewer, or in a store (mercantile) with 100 or fewer. Where only one toilet facility per sex is required, two unisex facilities may be used instead.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Exceptions: 1. Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. 2. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 30 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in all other structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including employees and customers, of 25 or fewer. 3. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. 4. Except as provided in Section 405.3.2. 5. Where the code requires only one toilet facility for each sex, two unisex facilities may be substituted for separate facilities. The delayed effective date of this Rule is January 1, 2021.

occupant_load.text: Building Code Table 1004.1.2: business areas 100 gross sq ft per occupant; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; classroom area 20 net. Public schools instead count 29 students per classroom (K-8) and 33 (9-12), with staff at 1.75 per classroom; private schools use the table.
occupant_load.quote: TABLE 1004.1.2 MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA ALLOWANCES PER OCCUPANT ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 100 gross ... Educational: Classroom area | 20 net. // 403.8.1 Occupant Content. Occupant content of public schools for the purpose of determining the number of required facilities shall be the maximum design class size multiplied by the number of classrooms. ... The maximum design class sizes are 29 students for grades K through 8 and 33 students for grades 9 through 12 (N.C.G.S. 115C-301). The occupant load for private schools shall be as listed in Table 1004.1.2 of the North Carolina Building Code.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. Office row: 1 per 30 for the first 30. 25/30 = 0.83, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals may replace no more than 50% of required toilets: 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 0.
50 per sex. 1 for the first 30, plus 20/50 = 0.4 for the remainder: 1.4, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
100 per sex. 1 for the first 30, plus 70/50 = 1.4: 2.4, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 per sex. 1 for the first 30, plus 170/50 = 3.4: 4.4, rounds up to 5 each. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 per sex. Restaurant row: 1 per 75. 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals may replace no more than 67% of required toilets in assembly: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.
50 per sex. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals: 0.
100 per sex. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 per sex. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.

Grades K-8 row, students only: 1 per 25 for each sex. 25/25 = 1 each. Grades 9-12 boys at 1 per 30: 25/30 = 0.83, also 1. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0. A public school group restroom needs at least four flushing fixtures (403.8.5.2), which is more than this table arithmetic.
K-8: 50 per sex, 50/25 = 2 each. Grades 9-12 boys: 50/30 = 1.67, rounds up to 2. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1. Public school group restrooms need at least four flushing fixtures each.

K-8: 100 per sex, 100/25 = 4 each. Grades 9-12 boys: 100/30 = 3.33, rounds up to 4. Urinals: 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2 (and a four-fixture male group restroom in a public school must keep at least two toilets).
K-8: 200 per sex, 200/25 = 8 each. Grades 9-12 boys: 200/30 = 6.67, rounds up to 7 (girls stay at 8). Urinals: 67% of 8 = 5.36, so 5 (67% of 7 = 4.69, so 4, for grades 9-12).

other_notes: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door (Plumbing Code 405.3.4; Building Code 1210.3.1); each urinal needs partitions starting no more than 12 in above the floor and reaching at least 60 in (405.3.5).
Public schools (403.8.5.2): 'Every public school group facility shall have a minimum of four flushing type fixtures. Four flushing male group toilets shall have a minimum of two water closets.'
Section 403.1 as amended applies the table 'In new construction or building additions and in changes of occupancy'.

hdpe_fire.section: 2018 North Carolina Building Code, Section 803.9 (with 803.1.2 and the Chapter 2 definition of interior wall and ceiling finish)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish it shall comply with Section 803.1.2. // 803.1.2 Room Corner Test for Interior Wall or Ceiling Finish Materials. Interior wall or ceiling finish materials shall be permitted to be tested in accordance with NFPA 286. Interior wall or ceiling finish materials tested in accordance with NFPA 286 shall comply with Section 803.1.2.1. // Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish. The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; and interior wainscoting, paneling or other finish applied structurally or for decoration ... but not including trim.
hdpe_fire.note: Read on UpCodes (secondary). The official OSFM list of Building Code amendments (through December 2024) contains no amendment to Section 803.9.

access.state_standard: Chapter 11 of the 2018 North Carolina Building Code, which requires ICC A117.1-2009 (Section 1101.2; Chapter 35 lists 'ICC A117.1-09'). UpCodes shows the standard as adopted without amendments. The federal 2010 ADA Standards apply alongside.

differences.point: Vertical grab bar on the side wall
differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 604.5.1, applied to wheelchair stalls by 604.9.6 and to both sides of ambulatory stalls by 604.10.4
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.5.1: 'The side wall grab bar shall be 42 inches (1065 mm) long minimum, located 12 inches (305 mm) maximum from the rear wall and extending 54 inches (1370 mm) minimum from the rear wall.' No vertical bar.
differences.quote: In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (455 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum above the floor, and with the center line of the bar located 39 inches (990 mm) minimum and 41 inches (1040 mm) maximum from the rear wall.

differences.state: ICC A117.1-2009 604.7: measured from the rear wall
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.7: 'Toilet paper dispensers shall comply with 309.4 and shall be 7 inches (180 mm) minimum and 9 inches (230 mm) maximum in front of the water closet measured to the centerline of the dispenser. The outlet of the dispenser shall be 15 inches (380 mm) minimum and 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum above the finish floor and shall not be located behind grab bars.'
differences.quote: Where the dispenser is located above the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 36 inches (915 mm) maximum from the rear wall. Where the dispenser is located below the grab bar, the outlet of the dispenser shall be located within an area 24 inches (610 mm) minimum and 42 inches (1065 mm) maximum from the rear wall. The outlet of the dispenser shall be located 18 inches (455 mm) minimum and 48 inches (1220 mm) maximum above the floor.

differences.point: Number of wheelchair stalls in a large restroom
differences.state: NC Building Code 1109.2.2: 5 percent of compartments
differences.federal: 2010 ADA 213.3.1: 'Where toilet compartments are provided, at least one toilet compartment shall comply with 604.8.1. In addition ... at least one compartment shall comply with 604.8.2 where six or more toilet compartments are provided, or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures.'
differences.quote: Where water closet compartments are provided in a toilet room or bathing room, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be wheelchair accessible. Where the combined total water closet compartments and urinals provided in a toilet room or bathing room is six or more, at least 5 percent of the total number of compartments shall be ambulatory accessible, provided in addition to the wheelchair-accessible compartment.

differences.federal: The 2010 ADA Standards have no requirement to provide a family or assisted-use toilet room (213.2 only covers the accessibility of rooms that are provided).
differences.quote: In assembly and mercantile occupancies, an accessible family or assisted-use toilet room shall be provided where an aggregate of six or more male and female water closets is required.

differences.federal: 2010 ADA 604.8.2.1: 'a depth of 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum and a width of 35 inches (890 mm) minimum and 37 inches (940 mm) maximum'
differences.quote: The minimum area of an ambulatory accessible compartment shall be 60 inches (1525 mm) minimum in depth and 36 inches (915 mm) in width.

access.same_as_federal: Wheelchair stall size (60 in wide; 56 in deep wall-hung, 59 in floor-mounted), toe clearance (9 in high, 6 in deep; 12 in for children's stalls), self-closing doors with pulls both sides, 42 in latch-side approach clearance read the same in A117.1-2009 604.9 and ADA 604.8.1. A117.1 604.9.3.1 also allows the door opening 56 in from the closet-side wall as an alternative; the ADA allows only 4 in from the far side wall, so follow the ADA position.
access.process: No separate state accessibility registration or state plan-review step was found on the OSFM site; accessibility is part of the State Building Code, which applies statewide. Not confirmed from an official page: ask the local inspections department (or OSFM Codes and Interpretations).

single_user.rule: No state law or code section requires a single-user restroom to be open to all genders or to carry an all-gender sign. Required public facilities must have signs designating the sex. A family or assisted-use room need not be identified for one sex, and where only one toilet facility per sex is required, two unisex facilities may replace the separate rooms.
single_user.quote: 403.4 Signage. Required public facilities shall be provided with signs that designate the sex, as required by Section 403.2. // 403.2.1 ... Family or assisted-use toilet facilities shall not be required to be identified for exclusive use by either sex as required by Section 403.4. // 403.2 Exception 5. Where the code requires only one toilet facility for each sex, two unisex facilities may be substituted for separate facilities.

all_gender_shared.rule: The 2018 NC Plumbing and Building Codes require separate facilities for each sex above the small-occupancy limits and contain no exception allowing a multi-stall all-gender room to count toward the required fixtures. Whether one can be approved (for example as an alternate method, or under the adopted but not yet effective 2024 code) is a question for the local inspections department. Every toilet must be in its own compartment with a door in any case.
all_gender_shared.quote: 403.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. // 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.

use_restrictions.rule: No state law in force restricts who may use which restroom. G.S. 143-760 (2016, single-sex multiple occupancy facilities in public agencies) was repealed in 2017. G.S. 143-761 bars state agencies, UNC, community colleges, cities, counties and school boards from regulating access to multiple occupancy restrooms except under an act of the General Assembly. 2025 bills S516 and H791 (restrooms by biological sex in covered facilities) were referred to committee and not enacted as of the bill pages read; S.L. 2025-84 (H805) covers school sleeping quarters, not restrooms.
use_restrictions.quote: § 143-761. Preemption of regulation of access to multiple occupancy restrooms, showers, or changing facilities. State agencies, boards, offices, departments, institutions, branches of government, including The University of North Carolina and the North Carolina Community College System, and political subdivisions of the State, including local boards of education, are preempted from regulation of access to multiple occupancy restrooms, showers, or changing facilities, except in accordance with an act of the General Assembly. (2017-4, s. 2.) // § 143-760: Repealed by Session Laws 2017-4, s. 1, effective March 30, 2017.

public_wage.quote: Twenty-four states do not have prevailing wage laws. These States are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas ... North Carolina, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Carolina ... (U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, 'Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage', last revised January 1, 2023). Federal: 'The Davis-Bacon and Related Acts apply to contractors and subcontractors performing on federally funded or assisted contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of public buildings or public works.'
public_wage.note: Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded or assisted work over $2,000. The DOL table is dated 2023; no NC Department of Labor page was read. Both DOL pages were read through WebFetch (direct download was blocked).

shipped_goods.rule: A remote seller must register and collect NC tax once its gross sales sourced to North Carolina exceed $100,000 in the previous or current calendar year. Otherwise the buyer owes use tax at the same rate on property bought outside the state for use in it.
shipped_goods.quote: A remote seller must register and collect sales and use tax when it is engaged in business in the state. This includes when the remote seller has gross sales in excess of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) sourced to North Carolina in the previous or current calendar year ("Threshold"), including sales as a marketplace seller and marketplace-facilitated sales. // G.S. 105-164.6(a): An excise tax at the applicable rate ... is imposed on ... (1) Tangible personal property purchased, leased, or rented inside or outside this State for storage, use, or consumption in this State. This subdivision includes tangible personal property that becomes part of a building or another structure.

freight.quote: (237) Sales price. - The total amount or consideration for which an item is sold, leased, or rented. ... a. The term includes all of the following: ... 4. Delivery charges. 5. Installation charges. // (49) Delivery charges. - Charges imposed by the retailer for preparation and delivery of an item to a location designated by the consumer.

install_labor.rule: Taxable as 'repair, maintenance, and installation services' at the state plus local rate, even when separately stated, when the job is an installation or like-for-like replacement on its own. Not taxed to the customer when the work qualifies as a capital improvement (see furnish_and_install).
install_labor.quote: The sales price of or the gross receipts derived from repair, maintenance, and installation services to real property, tangible personal property, motor vehicles, or certain digital property sold at retail and sourced to this state are subject to the general state, applicable local, and applicable transit rates of sales and use tax unless exempt by statute. ... Note: Installation charges are part of the definition of sales price. Installation charges are subject to sales and use tax, no matter that the installation charges may be separately stated by the retailer. ... To install, apply, connect, adjust, or set into position tangible personal property or certain digital property. The term includes floor refinishing and the installation of carpet, flooring, floor coverings, windows, doors, cabinets, countertops, and other installations where the item being installed may replace a similar existing item. ... The term does not include an installation defined and substantiated as a capital improvement.

furnish_and_install.rule: A contract for a capital improvement (new construction, reconstruction or remodeling; work needing a State Building Code permit; a fixture attached to real property that is capitalized and depreciated; a permanently affixed addition or alteration that is not a listed repair, maintenance and installation service) is a real property contract. The contractor is the consumer and pays tax on the materials; the contractor must not state tax separately on the invoice. Form E-589CI (Affidavit of Capital Improvement) substantiates it. Mixed contracts: if the taxable repair/installation part is 25% or less of the price, the whole is treated as a real property contract. NCDOR does not name toilet partitions; whether a stand-alone partition replacement is a capital improvement or a taxable installation is not stated.
furnish_and_install.quote: A real property contract is a contract between a real property contractor and another person to perform a capital improvement to real property. A transaction must meet the definition of a "capital improvement" to qualify as a real property contract. Generally, Form E-589CI, Affidavit of Capital Improvement, must be issued and kept on file for a real property contract. The sales and use tax applies to the sales price or purchase price of an item sold to a real property contractor for use by the real property contractor to fulfill a real property contract. The real property contractor is the consumer of the item that the real property contractor purchases, installs, or applies for others to fulfill a real property contract and that becomes part of real property or used to fulfill the contract. // G.S. 105-164.4H(c): An invoice or other documentation issued to a person by a real property contractor shall not separately state any amount for tax for a real property contract. // G.S. 105-164.3(31) Capital improvement. - One or more of the following: a. New construction, reconstruction, or remodeling. ... // (219) Remodeling. - A transaction comprised of multiple services performed by one or more persons to restore, improve, alter, or update real property ... The term does not include a single service that is included in repair, maintenance, and installation services.

rate_quote.quote: G.S. 105-164.4(a): The general rate of tax is four and three-quarters percent (4.75%).
rate_quote.note: Counties add local and transit rates; NCDOR's rates page lists 'Current Tax Rates (Effective July 1, 2026)' (city agent to read the county rate).

page.stalls_intro: North Carolina counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall with a door, and every urinal needs a privacy screen. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may take the place of up to half of the required toilets in an office, and up to 67% in a restaurant or school, so the table shows toilets only.
page.stalls_after: The school column counts students through grade 8; in grades 9 to 12 the boys' side needs 7 at 400. A public school counts its students by classroom, counts staff separately, and needs at least four toilets or urinals in each student group restroom. An office with 30 people or fewer, or any other space with 25 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms.
page.capacity: North Carolina's building rules count an office at one person per 100 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20, and a public school is counted at 29 students per classroom through grade 8 and 33 in grades 9 to 12.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** North Carolina's building rules count toilet partitions as an interior finish, and solid plastic (HDPE) or polypropylene used as an interior finish must pass a room-corner fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. A restroom with six or more toilets and urinals combined also needs a narrower stall with grab bars on both sides. Federal law and North Carolina's building rules set the sizes, and the state rules are the same in every city.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **North Carolina extras:** the state's rules add a vertical grab bar, at least 18 inches long, on the side wall of an accessible stall, which the federal rules don't ask for. They place the toilet paper holder by its distance from the back wall, and the federal rules place it by its distance from the front of the toilet, so the holder has to sit where both are met. In a large restroom, 5% of the stalls must be wheelchair accessible. Restaurants, theaters and stores that need six or more toilets must also have a family restroom.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** North Carolina's rules call for separate men's and women's restrooms, with signs, once a space holds more than 25 people (30 for an office, 100 for a store). Where each side needs only one toilet, two single-user rooms open to anyone may be used instead, and a family restroom doesn't have to be marked for one sex. The rules in force don't provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask your local building inspections department before planning one. State law leaves the question of who may use a multi-stall restroom to the General Assembly: state agencies, cities, counties and school boards may not set their own rules.
page.public_jobs: North Carolina has no state law setting wages on public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded or assisted projects over $2,000, under the federal Davis-Bacon Act.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in North Carolina, installation labor is taxed, even when it's billed separately, if the job is a repair, replacement or installation on its own. When the work is part of new construction, a remodel or another capital improvement, the contractor pays the tax on the materials and doesn't add sales tax to the contract, and normally keeps a signed capital improvement affidavit (Form E-589CI) on file.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, freight included. An out-of-state seller with more than $100,000 a year in North Carolina sales must collect the tax. If the seller doesn't collect it, the buyer owes use tax to the state at the same rate.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the North Carolina Department of Revenue
